key_insight: The paper turns diffusion models into in-context learners by conditioning the score function on a small set of task examples, allowing adaptation to unseen distributions without retraining.
engineering_relevance: This enables flexible generative modeling for scientific and vision tasks where each new scenario can be specified by a few samples instead of a full retraining pipeline.
method: Treat each target distribution as a task sampled from a meta-distribution and provide an empirical context set at inference.
Learn an in-context score operator that takes context samples, a noisy query point, and diffusion time to predict the task-dependent score.
Use a transformer-style query-dependent attention mechanism justified by a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean / Nadaraya–Watson representation.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on Navier-Stokes, ERA5 climate data, QuickDraw, and Food-101, showing strong results on simpler task families but weaker performance as task complexity increased.
watch_item: Performance can degrade on more complex task families, so context size, task diversity, and model capacity must be chosen carefully for reliable deployment.
paper_title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
